messages:
anne (arch): Heads-up — plan proposal to retire the legacy /v1/sync generate endpoint and fully move to streaming (/v2/stream) within 90 days. Proposing a temporary streaming->sync adapter for tenants that still call /v1/sync.

josh (eng-runtime): quick q: how will the adapter work? buffer whole stream->return single payload? memory concerns. :thinking:

anne (arch): yes, adapter buffers up to a configurable token/byte threshold (default 64kB). if threshold exceeded, adapter returns 502+hint or falls back to chunked partial response depending on tenant opt-in.

rachel (eng-platform): we should gate adapter via tenant flag + header so customers can opt in before we enable auto-fallback. header: `X-RW-Compat-Mode: stream-buffer`

josh (eng-runtime): runtime tradeoffs: buffering is straightforward but OOM risk for long-running LLM streams. we can implement per-request memory accounting and hard caps. also support incremental flush (emit final only when stream ends, else partial with `incomplete:true`).

kevin (sre): real concern: adapter increases tail latency and memory spike risk during burst. need circuit-breaker and SLO exemptions. add metrics for buffer_time_seconds and buffer_memory_bytes. alert on `buffer_memory_bytes > 0` p95 above threshold. :rotating_light:

marta (eng-infra): autoscaling implications: if many buffered requests, GPU pods might saturate memory. propose a separate pool label `buffer-adapter=true` to isolate capacity. also we can use kube QoS and oom_kill_protection settings.

josh (eng-runtime): implementation sketch: adapter sits in front of model worker and subscribes to stream frames, writes into an append-only buffer with streaming backpressure. When stream end -> compose final JSON and return. Pseudocode: 
```
// high level
buf = new RingBuffer(MAX_BYTES)
for frame in streamFrames() {
  if (buf.size + frame.size > MAX_BYTES) break; // enforce cap
  buf.append(frame)
}
if (streamEnded) return {text: buf.concat()}
else return {error: 'response truncated', partial: buf.concat()}
```

rachel (eng-platform): telemetry plan: instrument `compat.adapter.buffered_requests_total`, `compat.adapter.buffered_request_duration_seconds{quantile}`, `compat.adapter.oom_events`. dashboards per-tenant. PromQL example for p95 buffer time: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(compat_adapter_buffer_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant))`

kevin (sre): canary plan: start with internal tenants + 10 paid customers. gradual ramp using feature flag. if OOMs spike -> revert flag immediately. add emergency kill switch at edge router.

marta (eng-infra): infra ops: create autoscaling policy for `buffer-adapter=true` pool: scale by `compat.adapter.buffered_requests_total` and `gpu_mem_free_ratio`. Also set node eviction headroom.

anne (arch): API messaging: update docs, add deprecation banner on /v1/sync, provide migration snippet: 
```
# opt-in header to test adapter
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
     -H "X-RW-Compat-Mode: stream-buffer" \
     -d '{"prompt":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sync
```

josh (eng-runtime): fallback strategy: when buffer limit reached -> try 1) stream->compose with `partial:true` 2) route to smaller model variant that finishes sooner 3) return 429/provide migration guidance. prefer 2 for latency-sensitive apps.

rachel (eng-platform): rollout timeline proposal: week 0: internal dogfood + enable header for small cohort. week 2: expand to 10 customers. week 4: enable auto-fallback for low-risk tenants. week 12: soft-deprecate /v1/sync (announce removal date), week 16: remove.

kevin (sre): add observability runbook: on spike -> `kubectl cordon` new nodes, scale down adapter pool, enable `compat.off` global flag, notify customers via support.

anne (arch): decision checklist before soft-sunset: 
- metrics stable (buffer_time p95 < 500ms for canary)
- OOM rate ~ 0 for 7d
- customer migration guidance published
- infra autoscale in place

marta (eng-infra): note: we should also track cost delta per-token since buffering can add CPU/IO. add `compat.adapter_cpu_seconds_total` metric.

josh (eng-runtime): implementation note: prefer zero-copy frames and streaming KV cache rehydration to avoid duplicate memory. we should also honor model `max_new_tokens` to prevent runaway streams.

rachel (eng-platform): I'll draft the customer comms + SDK snippet for node/python showing how to convert sync calls to stream client with simple aggregator helper.

anne (arch): final: keep adapter for 90 days after public announcement, then remove if no major blockers. if blockers -> extend by 30-day windows only. anyone object?

kevin (sre): +1 with the emergency kill switch requirement.

josh (eng-runtime): +1. I'll start a PR for the adapter service and include the per-request accounting layer.

marta (eng-infra): +1. will prep autoscaling policy draft.

canary-bot: canary run started for tenant `internal-dogfood-01`. status: queued.

anne (arch): thanks all — I'll write RFC follow-up with runbook and rollout schedule. :thumbsup:
